close_reason: Landed in 8d12c8e. The four push_str(&format!(...)) sites that the bead named (originally in benches/mime_pipeline.rs; relocated by JMAP-t307.1 to tests/common/mod.rs) are now writeln!(s, ...).expect('writing to String') using std::fmt::Write. One intermediate String allocation eliminated per call.
description:
What the code does: crate-jmap-mime/benches/mime_pipeline.rs builds fixture byte strings by chaining `s.push_str(&format!("...", x))` four times — at lines 88, 143, 167, 185 (clippy pedantic `format_push_string` flags all four).

What idiomatic Rust would do: bring `std::fmt::Write` into scope and use `write!(s, "...", x).expect("writing to String never fails")` or `writeln!(...)`. This is the standard pattern for incrementally building a `String` with formatted content; `push_str(&format!(...))` allocates an intermediate `String` that is immediately copied and dropped.

Why it matters: this is a Rust practitioner instinct, not a style preference — clippy's pedantic `format_push_string` exists because (a) the extra allocation has measurable cost in hot code, (b) the `write!` form scales to multiple format args on one line without nesting, and (c) it composes with `?` in functions that return `Result`. In bench-fixture setup the perf delta is negligible (fixtures build once outside the timed `b.iter`), but the pattern is read as the canonical 'how to build a `String`' example by anyone learning from this code. Four instances is enough to set a local style; fixing them aligns with the rest of the bench file which uses bare `push_str` everywhere else.

Concrete sites:
- crate-jmap-mime/benches/mime_pipeline.rs:88 — `s.push_str(&format!("Content-ID: <part-{}@example.com>\\r\\n", idx));`
- crate-jmap-mime/benches/mime_pipeline.rs:143 — `s.push_str(&format!("Content-Type: multipart/mixed; boundary=\"{}\"\\r\\n", boundaries[0]));`
- crate-jmap-mime/benches/mime_pipeline.rs:167 — `out.push_str(&format!("Content-ID: <L{}-leaf-{}@example.com>\\r\\n", level + 1, leaf_idx));`
- crate-jmap-mime/benches/mime_pipeline.rs:185 — `out.push_str(&format!("Content-Type: multipart/mixed; boundary=\"{}\"\\r\\n", inner));`

Suggested fix:
```rust
use std::fmt::Write as _;
// ...
write!(s, "Content-ID: <part-{idx}@example.com>\\r\\n").expect("writing to String");
```

Out of scope: src/lib.rs is unchanged in scope; the adapter code does not use this pattern. The fix is entirely in benches/mime_pipeline.rs.
title: Bench builders use `s.push_str(&format!(...))` — should be `write!` via fmt::Write
